Nature Poems by Mitali Chakravarty Override? The rain falls in sheets of crinkled polythene. Mists rise like liquid ice. Modern similes catch on, plastinated, different from the past. Human constructs override nature. And yet, tsunamis swipe away mighty buildings with one tall wave. Floods submerge like Atlantis, a city where now fishes dream. Post-Pompeii, lava still burns, petrifies. Sea levels continue to rise in Venice. Djakarta will be replaced by Nusantara as overused, the land sinks. Earthquakes rock plates, destroying homes, people and what they make. Long ago, civilisations grew with the flow of rivers, with ebb of tides. And now? ~~ After a Downpour Yesterday, the rain obliterated the sky with loud words pattering down the pavement. The sound clattered till nothing could be heard except the drops, burdened by the weight of the world. Today, The grass is still wet. But it’s the words from birds that fill the universe. They fly, hop on grass, converse in large groups, watching the sun rise. The sun climbs higher. Some leave for work. Maybe, this afternoon, the rain will trot like horses. My window watches the trees. Dynasties over eons have rolled out carpets for blue stars that twinkle on the grass after a downpour. Sometimes the clouds make history with rain and birds continue to serenade. The Earth, over eons, looks on bemused.
